season_context.local_season_notes: Cool, damp winter from November to March, so coats, knits and textured outerwear lead sell-through. Christmas gifting and party wear peak in December. National winter sales run from 6 January to 2 February 2027 (2 January in four eastern departments). Spring/Summer 2027 stock lands from February to March.

From top-to-toe gold to bruised hues - the 7 standout trends from Paris Fashion Week SS27

trends.name: Tactile, shaggy textures
trends.summary: Shops are stocked with plush and hairy knits, brushed surfaces, bouclé wools, fuzzy cotton canvas and towelling-like terry. Relief and volume in the cloth itself are the main selling point of the season.

trends.name: 1990s outdoor and technical hybrids
trends.summary: Archive sportswear from labels such as Nike and K-Way is being reworked into everyday hybrid garments, giving technical outerwear a graphic, sporty-chic look for city wear.

trends.name: Boxy leather jacket
trends.summary: The leather jacket returns in roomier, squarer cuts made from smooth, cleanly finished hides. Unlike the usual fitted biker shape, these give more freedom of movement.

trends.name: Tartan, Prince of Wales and windowpane checks
trends.summary: Checks appear on coats, pleated or tailored skirts and shirts, and lumberjack-style shirts are often paired with tailored skirts. Paris runways also showed brighter 90s plaid, such as sky blue at Louis Vuitton and army green at Dries Van Noten.

trends.name: Faux fur coats and trims
trends.summary: Long-pile faux fur and curly shearling-style textures appear on statement coats with structured volume, and on smaller pieces such as collars and hats.

trends.name: Daytime sequins and pearls
trends.summary: Small sequins, beads and pearl details are moving off eveningwear and onto ordinary daywear, adding some polish to everyday garments.

trends.name: Craft and raw natural materials
trends.summary: Utilitarian garments use raw natural materials, visible handwork and sometimes wooden details, so each piece looks made by hand and one of a kind.

trends.name: Extreme drop waist
trends.summary: At Paris AW26, Chanel and Mugler pushed waistlines down to just above the knee, building on the wider shift toward low-waisted dresses.

trends.name: Tomato red
trends.summary: Tom Ford, Jean Paul Gaultier and Patou showed head-to-toe red, while Lacoste and Celine used it in smaller colour-blocked touches.

trends.name: Oversized face graphics
trends.summary: Acne Studios, Balenciaga and Ann Demeulemeester printed large human faces on dresses, skirts, blouses and T-shirts.

trends.name: Exaggerated 80s shoulders
trends.summary: Architectural jackets and coats with heavily built-up shoulders were prominent in the AW26 shows, including Saint Laurent, Balenciaga, Mugler, Tom Ford, Alaïa and Stella McCartney.

trends.name: Suits and ties return in menswear
trends.summary: Paris men's AW26 leaned on suits worn with ties. Louis Vuitton showed single- and double-breasted cuts and Glencheck suits, Dior showed both 1940s and 1960s tailoring, and the palette stayed mostly black, grey, beige and brown with violet accents.

trends.name: Couture arts-and-crafts embellishment
trends.summary: At July's AW26 couture shows, Chanel and Dior used beads, buttons, cut-outs and fabric loops, and Georges Hobeika showed dense, scale-like beadwork. The effect is collected, handmade ornament instead of conventional glamour.

trends.name: Paris Modest Fashion Week debut
trends.summary: Think Fashion held Paris's first modest fashion week in April 2026, with 30 shows and some French labels such as streetwear-influenced Soutoura. Headscarf debates in France make the segment politically sensitive.

trends.name: Year-round modest assortments
trends.summary: Retailers are told to plan around Ramadan and Eid for long, elegant dresses and to stock modest brands all year. Galeries Lafayette is named among department stores responding, though French-specific data is lacking.

trends.name: Kidswear in chocolate, ginger and ribbed velvet
trends.summary: A Paris kids concept store's AW26 edit uses chocolate, ginger, navy and ivory tones, needlecord, denim, fleece and intarsia knits, plus playful illustrated prints such as mushrooms and graphic flowers.

trends.name: Socks under heels and lace-trim street style
trends.summary: Paris SS27 street style showed socks worn with high heels, nodding to indie sleaze, and lace-edged camisoles over tailored trousers.

trends.name: Graphics and slogans
trends.summary: Dries Van Noten printed vintage-style movie posters, while Celine, Sacai, Marine Serre and Stella McCartney showed slogan or graphic T-shirts. Acne Studios showed graphic denim.

trends.name: Citrus orange and bruised purples
trends.summary: Hermès, Chanel, Loewe and Mugler showed orange, while lilac and royal purple appeared at Chanel, Longchamp and Miu Miu. All-gold looks at Saint Laurent and head-to-toe single colours were also key.

trends.name: Rococo revival
trends.summary: Acne Studios, Schiaparelli, Valentino and Vivienne Westwood revisited the 18th century with nipped waists, ruffles, lace, brocade, velvet and watercolour florals, styled with modern pieces.

trends.name: Edwardian drop waist and corsetry at Chanel
trends.summary: Matthieu Blazy's second Chanel ready-to-wear show drew on Coco Chanel's Edwardian childhood. Soft 1920s low-waisted shapes appeared alongside structured, corseted bodices.

trends.name: Weightless layers and trailing skirts
trends.summary: Dior, Chanel and Aje used airy, delicate layers and long trailing skirts. L'Agence showed a featherweight trench.

trends.name: Reworked denim
trends.summary: Ujoh deconstructed and layered denim, Zimmermann styled a denim dress formally, and Miu Miu's Wrangler collaboration added hand-customised crisscross lacing.

trends.name: Pinstripe shirt as a staple
trends.summary: Dior paired asymmetric-collar pinstripe shirts with tiered floral skirts, and Tom Ford, Givenchy, Carven and Acne also used the pinstripe shirt. Pink or brown stripes keep it from looking nautical.

trends.name: Glamour goth
trends.summary: Ann Demeulemeester used black lace, sheer fabrics and leather, Dior and Balmain used shredded hems and ruffles, and Ester Manas showed lingerie-inspired black looks for summer.

trends.name: Première Vision SS27 key shades
trends.summary: Première Vision's SS27 palette centres on a grounded brown, a lively organic green, a light effervescent yellow that is growing in women's dresses and tops, and a regenerative white.

trends.name: Deep violet, plum and gender-neutral pink
trends.summary: At Première Vision Paris in September 2026, deep violet with cool yellow highlights led the colour story. Plum and deep red were offered as alternatives to black, neutrals shifted toward blue-grey and taupe, and pink and mauve moved into menswear.

trends.name: Double-face weaves, jacquards and performance suiting
trends.summary: Mills are reviving separable double-cloth wools for reversible, seam-free finishes, alongside tapestry and jacquard heritage. Suiting cloth is adding hidden waterproof membranes and bi-stretch so it keeps its tailored look.

trends.name: Evening fabrics and ultrafine wool
trends.summary: Satins, crushed velvets and wool blends borrowed from eveningwear are prominent. Very fine yarns and tight knits make wool feel as soft as silk or cotton, and mossy or fur-effect surfaces add texture.

trends.name: Kids SS27: red, navy and nautical stripes
trends.summary: Playtime Paris SS27 buyers saw red in bright and deep shades, navy with maritime themes, multidirectional stripes, sailor collars and a stronger, more varied use of denim in kidswear.
